A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NaLaFormer and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A.1–A.9. Content can be matched across the layout changes and renumbering without material evidence gaps.

before.justification: V2 reports original NaLaFormer results for classification, detection, segmentation, super-resolution, diffusion, language modeling, and LRA, together with appendix ablations.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results and adds super-resolution comparisons, Manga109 results, and a QK-Norm control experiment.

M1.justification: Section 4.4 adds a DCTLSA-based, patch-wise super-resolution model alongside the existing ESRT-based NaLaSR, now also called NaLa-ESRT. This is a limited architectural adaptation; the norm-dependent power map, cosine-direction kernel, and gating mechanism remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V3 Table 20 extends super-resolution evaluation to Manga109 at ×3 and ×4. The other datasets and tasks remain covered. The ×3 scenario itself is not new: it already appeared in v2 Table 15.

E2.justification: V3 substantially expands super-resolution comparisons with SwinIR and DCTLSA in Tables 4/20 and VDSR, MemNet, and SRMDNF in Table 19. It also adds QK-Norm as a normalization control in Table 15 and CA to the Swin-T attention comparison in Table 9. The earlier comparator sets are otherwise retained.

E3.justification: V3 introduces DCTLSA-based super-resolution configurations and RTX3090 efficiency measurements, plus a QK-Norm/FLatten/NaLaFormer comparison using matched configurations within Swin and PVT backbones. These are additional evaluation designs, not evidence that the retained experiments were rerun. Exact configurations for the new QK-Norm comparison remain underspecified.

E4.justification: Sections 4.8 and A.3 add a QK-Norm control to test whether normalization alone explains the gains. The component, architectural-component, and τ/λ ablations already existed in v2; their appearance in the new main-text ablation section largely redisplays existing evidence.

E5.justification: Benchmark tables retain point-estimate reporting, without added repeated-run counts, seed information, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates. The existing entropy-correlation plots are retained.

E6.justification: V3 adds substantial super-resolution accuracy and efficiency results, QK-Norm control results, and CA's 82.2% accuracy. For example, its new Manga109 ×4 comparison reports 31.43 dB for the DCTLSA-based NaLa variant versus 31.04 for DCTLSA. Most retained results match, but v2 Table 15's ×3 ESRT/NaLaSR latency and memory rows are removed. The added model results are not same-setting revisions of the earlier NaLaSR scores.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 retains the PSE definition, both entropy theorems, and their proofs despite renumbering. V3's S and Z intermediate quantities abbreviate the existing attention-output computation; they do not introduce a new theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central query-norm cancellation diagnosis, norm-aware/cosine-direction solution, and multimodal accuracy-efficiency claims. The headline 7.5% accuracy, 4.7% mIoU, and 92.3% memory figures remain unchanged; the additional experiments mainly support the existing contribution.

C2.justification: V3 newly interprets the QK-Norm comparison as evidence that gains exceed normalization effects and discusses bounded norm restoration in relation to training stability. Appendix A.6 adds prospective VLM/compression integration and larger-scale validation. The existing limitations paragraph remains unchanged, and the new comparison does not document a large-scale stability study.

D1.justification: V3 replaces the supplementary-material code pointer with a repository hyperlink, identifies RTX3090 hardware for the new SR timings, and adds an FLA reference with access information. Conversely, A.2 removes the previously stated 40,000/160,000 training iterations for SemanticFPN/UperNet. This is a documentation loss, not an explicitly changed training budget.

R1.justification: V3 adds references supporting the new SR and CA comparisons, Skyformer, FLA, and positional-encoding/VLM future directions. It removes the SlimPajama citation while retaining the dataset. Anonymous (2026) and Meng et al. (2026) refer to the same MirrorLA work; the central positioning against existing linear attention remains stable.

P1.justification: Most prose is retained. V3 rewrites the SR results discussion, moves efficiency analysis after diffusion and language modeling, adds a main-text ablation summary, and introduces acknowledgments and an impact statement. These are localized narrative and structural changes.

P2.justification: V3 replaces the branded single-column main paper with a two-column conference layout, changing typography, headers, theorem boxes, and many figure/table placements and sizes. It restructures the SR tables, adds the QK-Norm table, and redisplays appendix ablations in the main text. The plotted data and image examples remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new normalization control and DCTLSA/SwinIR comparisons, including Manga109, provide a modest net improvement in empirical support; the repository link also improves access instructions. These benefits are tempered by limited configuration details for the additions and the removal of segmentation training budgets and earlier ×3 ESRT efficiency results. The core theory and most original findings remain unchanged.
